Regulation actions in collaborative learning, as sequences

Source: R/data-group_regulation.R
group_regulation.Rd

group_regulation is a coded dataset, in wide format, of regulation during collaborative learning: each row is one sequence of coded actions and each column an ordered position. The nine actions are adapt, cohesion, consensus, coregulate, discuss, emotion, monitor, plan and synthesis. Sequences are 2 to 26 actions long; shorter sequences are padded with NA.

With nine states and 2,000 sequences, the data give a dense transition table in which most transitions depart from independence, and they are used to show lag transition networks and group comparisons. The same actions are available as an event log in group_regulation_long.

Usage

group_regulation

Format

A data frame with 2,000 rows (sequences) and 26 character columns T1 to T26 (positions, in order).

Source

Identical to tna::group_regulation (tna package, MIT license).

See also

group_regulation_long for the event log; engagement; lsa().

Examples

fit <- lsa(group_regulation)
transitions(fit, direction = "over", sort = "strength") |> head()
